assessment_summary: I validated the Qisutu installation against the supplied Installation.md by inspecting state files, database, system services, and — most importantly — exercising the application over HTTP. (1) Instance artifacts: /opt/qisutu/var/install/instance.conf matches every auto-derived value the guide specifies for the /opt/qisutu path (web_path, Apache file, daemon service, QISUTU_SESSION cookie, db name/user, language de), and installed.lock exists with the expected metadata. (2) Web functionality: I fetched the login page (200), posted the generated admin credentials with the page's own CSRF token and Step=Login/AccountType=agent fields — the server responded 302 and set a QISUTU_SESSION cookie, and the resulting session rendered the agent portal dashboard, proving the full request stack (Apache CGI + Perl + MariaDB + session handling) works end-to-end. A negative login with a wrong password was rejected with no session cookie. install.pl correctly reports 'bereits installiert'. (3) Database: 138 live tables exactly match the 138 CREATE TABLE statements in install/sql/schema.sql; database_version=2.0.2; the admin user_account row exists (local auth, active); the DB user qisutu has scoped ALL PRIVILEGES on qisutu.* only; the temporary bootstrap DB user was deleted after setup, as the guide describes. (4) System components: Apache site qisutu.conf is enabled with the correct ScriptAlias and serving on port 80; MariaDB listens on 3306; only qisutu-daemon.service remains in /etc/systemd/system (temporary install-complete path/service units were removed exactly as the guide's 'temporäre Abschlussdienste' section requires); the daemon process runs as user qisutu (group www-data) with the unit's ExecStart line; Perl modules Authen::SASL, Net::LDAP, DBI load; var/secure/security.key exists; the install log records the successful DB/system/completion steps and contains no passwords. (5) Guard behavior: re-running install.sh refuses to modify the completed instance. Limitations: the container has no running systemd, so units are managed via the documented systemctl shim; I could verify unit files, enable-state, and the correct process/user but not systemd-native boot-time path-unit triggering. Mail configuration was intentionally skipped, which the guide explicitly permits. No discrepancies or broken components were found; the installation is complete and operational per the guide.
